plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding higher than my value only risks overpaying if I win, and bidding lower only risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $14, I should bid exactly $14 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid here, unlike first-price auctions. Thus, I will bid my true value of $34 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you pay the second-highest bid only if you win, so bidding your value maximizes expected profit regardless of others' actions. Overbidding risks negative profit; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $33, I should bid exactly $33 to ensure optimal outcome given the mechanism.
